digest.top_line: STELLAR: 5x5 Gy + CAPOX noninferior for 3y DFS (64.5% v 62.3%, HR 0.883) with 3y OS 86.5% v 75.1% (HR 0.67), LRR 8.4% v 11.0%.
digest.tldr: Two Chinese phase 3 TNT trials land on the same read: short-course or long-course, the RT arm buys distant control, not local control. STELLAR LRR 8.4% v 11.0% (NS) and TNTCRT locoregional failure 6.03% v 6.19% (P=.943) both say pelvic control is already saturated; the DFS gain is metastatic. Lower GI carried the day; prostate contributed two PSMA PET imaging talks, neither a dataset that moves an RT decision.

sites.intro: Two phase 3 TNT trials with LCRT or 5x5 Gy in the experimental arm, both reporting locoregional failure flat against the comparator.

studies.name: TNTCRT
studies.tldr: 3-yr DFS 74.8% v 66.0%, HR 0.674, for doublet-CAPOX TNT vs nCRT in high-risk LARC; locoregional failure unchanged.

details: 🔍 Phase 3, N=458 (232 v 226), accrued 2017-2023, median f/u 51 mo, age 18-70

subdetails: TNT: induction CAPOX x1 → LCRT + concurrent CAPOX x2 → consolidation CAPOX x3 → TME
nCRT: LCRT + concurrent capecitabine → TME → adjuvant CAPOX x6 at 4-8 wks

details: 📐 LCRT in both arms; RT dose, fractionation, target volume not reported in source text
⚠️ DFS gain rests on distant control; OS curves have not separated at 3 years
⚠️ Age capped at 70; author states benefit-risk above that needs further study

verdict.rationale: Randomized phase 3, primary DFS met at 51-mo median f/u, but TNT is already established by RAPIDO/PRODIGE-23/STELLAR; adds a regimen option, not a paradigm.

studies.significance: Locoregional failure was identical (6.03% v 6.19%, P=.943) with the entire chemo course moved preoperatively, so intensifying systemic therapy around LCRT costs nothing in local control. RT dose, fractionation and target volume are absent from the source text, which gates transfer. The decision this moves is chemo sequencing, not RT technique.
studies.monday_clinic: In high-risk stage II/III rectal cancer aged 70 or under with cT4, cN2, involved mesorectal fascia, or EMVI, this supports delivering the full CAPOX course before surgery rather than adjuvantly; it does not extend to pts over 70 or to stage II/III disease without a high-risk MRI feature.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Multicenter **randomized phase 3**, N=458, accrual June 2017 to December 2023, median follow-up **51 months**. Blinding is not stated in the source.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: Stage II/III LARC aged **18 to 70** with at least 1 MRI high-risk feature (cT4a-b, cN2, involved mesorectal fascia, or cT3c-d with EMVI). Baseline burden was heavy on every axis, with **cN2 in 75.98%** and a **threatened MRF in 70.96%**.

analysis_sections.label: Regimen
analysis_sections.body: Doublet-LC TNT: **1 cycle induction CAPOX**, LCRT with **2 cycles concurrent CAPOX**, **3 cycles consolidation CAPOX**, then surgery. Control: LCRT with **concurrent capecitabine**, surgery, then **6 cycles adjuvant CAPOX** starting 4 to 8 weeks postoperatively.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: **LCRT in both arms**, so radiotherapy is held constant and the randomization tests chemotherapy intensity and sequencing around it. **Dose, fractionation and target volume are not reported in the source text.** Roughly **87%** of TNT pts and **90%** of nCRT pts went on to total mesorectal excision.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: **Primary: disease-free survival.** Secondary endpoints included MFS, pCR, locoregional failure, overall survival, and toxicity across the neoadjuvant phase and the whole treatment course.

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: The excess grade ≥3 toxicity is confined to the **neoadjuvant phase**; across the full treatment course, and for major postoperative complications, the arms converge, because the control arm pays its chemotherapy cost after surgery instead.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: The source names **RAPIDO, PRODIGE-23 and STELLAR** as the phase 3 TNT precedents but reports no cross-trial numbers. The phase 2 precursor of this regimen reported a complete response rate of **36.2%**.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents high-risk stage II/III LARC aged 18 to 70 with cT4, cN2, involved mesorectal fascia, or EMVI. Does not represent pts over 70, or stage II/III disease carrying no high-risk MRI feature.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: The DFS interval reaches **0.929** and OS shows no separation, so the benefit rests on distant control with a modest margin. Late toxicity, function and quality of life are still pending per the authors, which matters for a regimen whose whole cost is delivered upfront.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: Locoregional failure was identical (6.03% v 6.19%), so moving the whole CAPOX course preoperatively costs nothing in local control while pCR rises to 26.37%, enlarging the pool for a watch-and-wait discussion. RT dose, fractionation and target volume are absent from the source text, which gates transfer.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: The variable here is chemotherapy, not radiotherapy: uninterrupted doublet CAPOX delivered entirely before surgery beat capecitabine chemoRT plus 6 adjuvant CAPOX cycles on DFS and MFS. The excess grade ≥3 toxicity sits in the neoadjuvant phase only and converges across the full course.
significance_by_specialty.surgonc: Intensified preoperative therapy did not degrade the operation: major postoperative complications were 3.98% v 2.94%, and roughly 87% versus 90% of pts proceeded to total mesorectal excision. The pCR jump to 26.37% is the number that will drive organ-preservation conversations at MDT.

studies.name: STELLAR
studies.tldr: 3y DFS 64.5% v 62.3% noninferior (HR 0.883) for 5x5 Gy plus CAPOX v long-course CRT; OS 86.5% v 75.1%.
details: 🔍 Multicenter open-label phase III, N=599, 16 Chinese hospitals, 1:1, distal/middle-third cT3-4 and/or cN+ LARC
🔍 1° EP 3y DFS, noninferiority margin HR 1.43, one-sided alpha 0.05, median f/u 35.0 mo
🔍 All pts received IMRT; CTV covered mesorectum, presacral space, internal iliac, obturator nodes, ischiorectal fossa; external iliac only if cT4b
📊 pCR + sustained cCR 21.8% TNT v 12.3% CRT, P = .002; cCR 11.1% v 4.4%
📊 R0 resection 91.5% v 87.8%, P = .189; grade III+ surgical complications 14.0% v 15.7%, P = .625

details.text: ⚠️ Acute grade 3-4 toxicity during preoperative treatment, by event

details: ⚠️ Preop completion 82.6% v 95.2% and full-dose completion 74.8% v 93.2%, both P < .001, favoring CRT
🔗 3y LRR (8.4% / 11.0%) in line with RAPIDO and PRODIGE 23 (4%-8.3%), far below Polish II (21%-22%)
⚠️ OS was secondary and unadjusted for multiplicity; subgroup analysis showed no significant OS difference, and the Polish II OS gain vanished by 8y
⚠️ 53 pts (17 TNT, 36 CRT) refused surgery for personal reasons and 28 v 10 went to watch-and-wait, so surgical rates are not protocol-driven

verdict.rationale: Randomised phase III meeting its prespecified noninferiority primary endpoint, consistent with Polish II and RAPIDO. OS gain was secondary, unadjusted, and not reproduced in subgroups.
verdict.audience: Distal/middle-third rectal adenocarcinoma, cT3-4 and/or cN+, ECOG 0-1, age 18-70

studies.significance: 5x5 Gy delivered with IMRT and a CTV excluding external iliacs unless cT4b gave 3y LRR 8.4%, so short-course loses nothing locoregionally while cutting RT to one week. The cost is front-loaded: grade 3-4 hematologic toxicity 15.8% v 2.0%, driven by the four CAPOX cycles, not the radiation.
studies.monday_clinic: In cT3-4 or node-positive middle or low rectal cancer where compressing preoperative RT to one week matters, this supports 5x5 Gy plus CAPOX as an alternative to 50 Gy/25 with capecitabine; it does not speak to upper-third tumors, which were excluded.

primary_endpoint.name: 3-year disease-free survival
primary_endpoint.stat_detail: HR 0.883, one-sided 95% CI to 1.11, P < .001 noninferiority

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Multicenter open-label randomized phase III at 16 hospitals across 11 Chinese provinces, 1:1, stratified by location, clinical stage and MRF status. **N = 599** (TNT 302, CRT 297), median follow-up **35.0 months**. Powered for noninferiority at a margin of **HR 1.43** with 194 DFS events.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: Age **18-70**, ECOG 0-1, **cT3-4 and/or node-positive** rectal adenocarcinoma of the distal or middle third, no distant metastases and no prior anticancer treatment. Baseline was balanced: cT4 15.9% v 12.8%, MRF involvement 56.3% v 56.2%, EMVI 53.4% v 42.1%.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: TNT arm **5 Gy x 5 over 1 week**; CRT arm **50 Gy in 25 fractions over 5 weeks** with concurrent capecitabine 825 mg/m2 BID. **All patients received IMRT**, unlike RAPIDO, Polish II and PRODIGE 23. CTV covered mesorectum, presacral space, internal iliac, obturator nodes and ischiorectal fossa, superior border at the sacral promontory, inferior border 2-3 cm below the tumor, external iliacs added only for **cT4b**; PTV expansion 0.5-1.0 cm.

analysis_sections.label: Regimen
analysis_sections.body: TNT: four cycles of CAPOX (oxaliplatin 130 mg/m2 day 1, capecitabine 1,000 mg/m2 BID days 1-14) starting **7-14 days after RT**, then TME, then two further CAPOX cycles. CRT: chemoradiotherapy, TME, then **six** cycles of CAPOX. Surgery was scheduled 6-8 weeks after preoperative treatment in both arms.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: **Primary: 3-year DFS**, noninferiority. Secondary: OS, MFS, locoregional recurrence, surgical complications, toxicity and completion rate. LRR was analyzed with competing-risks methods treating death without LRR as a competing risk.

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: Acute grade III-V toxicity during preoperative treatment **26.5% v 12.6%** (P < .001), driven by hematologic events (15.8% v 2.0%). Grade III+ surgical complications were similar (14.0% v 15.7%, P = .625) with no 30-day postoperative deaths; delayed wound healing predominated. Grade III-IV toxicity on adjuvant chemotherapy was **lower** with TNT (3.3% v 11.8%, P = .003).

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: Third randomized trial of short-course RT plus chemotherapy against long-course CRT after Polish II and RAPIDO. LRR of 8.4% and 11.0% matched RAPIDO and PRODIGE 23 (**4%-8.3%**) and beat Polish II (**21%-22%**); grade 3+ toxicity of 26.5% sat below RAPIDO's six-cycle CAPOX/FOLFOX and PRODIGE 23's FOLFIRINOX (approximately 47%). Unlike RAPIDO and PRODIGE 23, distant metastasis was not reduced.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents middle and distal-third cT3-4 or node-positive rectal cancer in patients age 18-70 with ECOG 0-1 treated with IMRT. Does not represent upper-third rectal tumors, recurrent disease, patients over 70, or the unresectable fixed cT3/cT4 population that dominated Polish II.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: The OS difference was a secondary endpoint without multiplicity adjustment, was not reproduced across subgroups, and the analogous Polish II OS gain disappeared at 8 years. The authors concede the **1.43 noninferiority margin was wide** in retrospect. 53 patients without cCR declined surgery for personal reasons (17 TNT v 36 CRT), an asymmetry that leaks into DFS.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: 5x5 Gy with IMRT and an internal-iliac/obturator CTV (external iliacs only for cT4b) gave 3y LRR 8.4% v 11.0%, so compressing RT from 5 weeks to 1 costs nothing locoregionally. Every patient completed RT without dose reduction, versus 1.4% reductions and 2.4% interruptions with 50 Gy/25.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: Moving CAPOX preoperatively raised planned-cycle completion (60.0% v 48.3%, P = .009) and cut adjuvant grade III-IV toxicity to 3.3% v 11.8%, but four preop cycles drove grade 3-4 hematologic toxicity to 15.8% v 2.0%. Unlike RAPIDO, 3y MFS was unchanged (77.1% v 75.3%).

sites.intro: Both entries are PSMA PET imaging talks (response assessment, BCR natural history), not therapeutic trials.

studies.name: USPCC 2026: PSMA PET Has No Role at Present as a Response Assessment
studies.tldr: Point-counterpoint: AR-axis therapy dynamically alters PSMA expression, so serial uptake change is prognostic but not yet a validated response metric.
details: 🔍 USPCC 2026 point-counterpoint talk (Steven Rowe, UT Southwestern), not a new dataset
🔬 Core argument: PSMA expression is androgen-regulated, so post-ADT uptake change may reflect AR signaling, not tumor burden

details.text: 📊 Zukotynski J Nucl Med 2021: 18F-DCFPyL PET before and 2-4mo after abiraterone/enzalutamide, N=16 evaluable
subdetails: Overall median time to therapy change 9.6mo (95% CI 6.9-14.2)
Mixed but predominantly increased uptake pattern → shorter time to therapy change and shorter OS

details.text: 📐 Zukotynski: outcomes by δ-SUVmax metric (low vs high)

details: ⚠️ N=16 with CIs spanning 1.17 to 47.87: prognostic separation is real but the point estimates are unstable
💊 Markowski J Nucl Med 2021: 6 men on bipolar androgen therapy, baseline + 3mo PSMA PET; 3 progressed on imaging, detected earlier than conventional imaging
🔍 Repeatability work (Bland-Altman, ICC, within-subject CV) on SUVmax/SUVmean/SUVtotal/tumor volume; lesion identification and segmentation variability persists even for lesions >1.5cm³
🔗 RECIP 1.0 (Gafita, J Nucl Med 2022) integrates PET with CT for PD/PR/SD/CR after radioligand therapy; presenter's read is that it needs further validation before routine use
⚠️ Takeaway as delivered: uptake change after AR-targeted therapy is unpredictable, and lesion-detection robustness plus AI-assisted segmentation are the gating problems
studies.significance: For RT and radioligand practice, the operational point is that a post-therapy rise in SUVmax is not interpretable as progression: it may be AR-driven flare in expression. RECIP 1.0 exists for the post-radioligand setting but the presenter treats it as unvalidated outside trials, so retreatment or salvage-RT decisions should not hinge on serial PSMA PET alone.
studies.monday_clinic: In mCRPC restaged with PSMA PET 2-4 months after starting abiraterone or enzalutamide, this argues that rising uptake alone does not establish progression; it does not address baseline staging PSMA PET, where the tracer's role is not in dispute.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: Bears on metastasis-directed and salvage RT triggered by serial PSMA PET: a new or brighter lesion on ARSI may be expression flare rather than true progression, so a lesion-by-lesion RT decision made off a post-treatment scan carries interpretive risk. RECIP 1.0 is post-radioligand and unvalidated here.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: Speaks to when to abandon an ARSI. Serial δ-SUVmax was prognostic (OS HR 5.03 for DPSM, 9.31 for DASM) but from N=16, so it should not drive a switch decision; PSA and conventional imaging remain the operative triggers, with BAT the one setting where PET flagged progression earlier.

studies.name: PSMA PET in Biochemically Recurrent Prostate Cancer (Natural History Study)
studies.tldr: Baseline data on 130 pts: most with PSA doubling time >9-12mo still had PSMA PET findings once PSA exceeded 5.
details: 🔍 Prospective NCI natural-history cohort; baseline data on the first 130 pts, GU-ASCO 2026
🔍 Enrolled post-definitive-therapy BCR, prior salvage RT or declined it, PSA ≥0.5 to be eligible
🔍 Baseline PET; if negative, annual imaging; any finding including equivocal, every 6 months
📊 Most pts with PSADT >9mo and >12mo still had PSMA PET findings once PSA exceeded 5
📊 Lesions seen: nodal disease, prostate-bed recurrence, small equivocal bone foci
📊 Only about a third have started therapy; the majority are observed off treatment
📊 Companion NCI poster: 5 of the first ~150 progressed on conventional imaging at ~1.5yr
📊 >95% had no abrupt PET change discordant with their PSA or PSA doubling time
⚠️ Therapy not mandated (intermittent ADT, ARPI trials, SBRT, Ra-223 allowed), so the history is partly treated

verdict.rationale: Baseline cross-sectional read from an ongoing observational cohort; no outcome data yet, median f/u about 2 years and longitudinal PET evolution not reported.
verdict.audience: PSMA-positive BCR after definitive therapy incl salvage RT, PSA ≥0.5

studies.significance: Detection is not the same as threat: PSMA positivity was near-universal in slow doubling-time pts (>9 and >12 months) once PSA passed 5, yet a companion poster found only 5 of the first ~150 progressed on conventional imaging at ~1.5 years. That gates the SBRT-to-oligomets versus observation call.
studies.monday_clinic: In men with PSMA-positive BCR after definitive therapy and prior salvage RT, PSA ≥0.5 with a doubling time over 9 to 12 months, this is evidence that a positive scan alone does not reclassify them as conventionally metastatic; it does not extend to pts with conventional-imaging metastases or those already on protocol therapy.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Prospective NCI natural-history protocol, still accruing. Baseline PSMA PET data on the first **130 pts** were reported; median follow-up is about **2 years**, with longitudinal analysis pending.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: BCR after definitive therapy, all of whom had already received **salvage radiation** or declined it. **PSA ≥0.5** was required to enroll.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: Every enrollee was post-definitive therapy including salvage RT. On study, **SBRT** is permitted, as is any therapy lasting **under six months**, alongside intermittent ADT and intermittent ARPI or Ra-223 trials.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: The reported analysis is descriptive at a single timepoint: baseline PSMA PET findings set against **PSA doubling time**, the field's working risk metric in BCR.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: Even at **PSADT >9 and >12 months**, the majority had PSMA PET findings once PSA exceeded **5**: nodal disease, prostate-bed recurrence, and small equivocal bone foci. About **a third** have gone on therapy; **>95%** showed no abrupt PET change out of step with PSA kinetics.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents PSMA-positive BCR after definitive therapy and salvage RT, PSA ≥0.5, largely observed off therapy. Does not represent conventional-imaging metastatic disease or pts who have not yet had salvage RT.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: The detection claim is anchored to **PSA above 5**, above the window where most salvage RT decisions are actually made, so it does not transfer downward. The progression count comes from a **companion poster** with a different subset and follow-up, not this analysis.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: Prostate-bed recurrence and nodal disease were among the lesions seen, so a positive PET here is often a pelvic or bed salvage question rather than a systemic one. Detection was near-universal only above PSA 5, above the window where most salvage RT decisions get made.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: About a third started therapy and the rest were observed, with 5 of roughly 150 progressing on conventional imaging at ~1.5 years. That argues against reflex mCSPC-style doublet or triplet intensification on PET findings alone in slow doubling-time pts.

papers.title: Total Neoadjuvant Therapy With Long-Course Radiotherapy Versus Chemoradiotherapy in High-Risk Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer (TNTCRT): A Multicenter, Randomized, Phase III Trial
papers.abstract: PURPOSE High-risk locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC) carries a substantial risk of distant recurrence, which limits disease-free survival (DFS). We compared total neoadjuvant therapy (TNT) integrating long-course radiotherapy (LCRT) with uninterrupted doublet chemotherapy (doublet-LC TNT) versus conventional neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (nCRT). METHODS In this multicenter, randomized, phase III trial, patients with stage II/III LARC and at least 1 high-risk feature (cT4a-b, cN2, mesorectal fascia involvement, or cT3c-d with extramural vascular invasion) were enrolled. Patients were assigned to doublet-LC TNT (induction, concurrent, and consolidation capecitabine plus oxaliplatin with LCRT) before surgery or nCRT (capecitabine with LCRT) followed by surgery and adjuvant chemotherapy. The primary end point was DFS (ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT03177382 ). RESULTS Between June 6, 2017, and December 27, 2023, 458 patients were randomly assigned to doublet-LC TNT (n = 232) or nCRT (n = 226). At a median follow-up of 51 months, doublet-LC TNT improved 3-year DFS (74.8% v 66.0%; hazard ratio [HR], 0.674 [95% CI, 0.489 to 0.929]; P = .016). Metastasis-free survival (MFS; 77.7% v 67.6%; HR, 0.655 [95% CI, 0.469 to 0.915]) and pathologic complete response rates (pCR; 26.37% v 9.80%; P < .001) were higher with doublet-LC TNT, whereas locoregional failure remained low and comparable (6.03% v 6.19%; P = .943). Although grade ≥3 adverse events during the neoadjuvant phase were more frequent with doublet-LC TNT (27.59% v 8.56%; P < .001), severe toxicities during the entire treatment course (28.02% v 24.32%; P = .371) and major postoperative complications (3.98% v 2.94%; P = .567) were comparable. CONCLUSION Compared with conventional nCRT, doublet-LC TNT improved DFS, MFS, and pCR rates with manageable toxicity. These findings support this intensified, doublet-based regimen as a standard option within the modern TNT paradigm. Further comparative studies are warranted to evaluate these results against other short-course radiotherapy‑based or nondoublet-concurrent TNT regimens.

papers.title: Multicenter, Randomized, Phase III Trial of Short-Term Radiotherapy Plus Chemotherapy Versus Long-Term Chemoradiotherapy in Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer (STELLAR)
papers.abstract: PURPOSE To ascertain if preoperative short-term radiotherapy followed by chemotherapy is not inferior to a standard schedule of long-term chemoradiotherapy in patients with locally advanced rectal cancer. MATERIALS AND METHODS Patients with distal or middle-third, clinical primary tumor stage 3-4 and/or regional lymph node–positive rectal cancer were randomly assigned (1:1) to short-term radiotherapy (25 Gy in five fractions over 1 week) followed by four cycles of chemotherapy (total neoadjuvant therapy [TNT]) or chemoradiotherapy (50 Gy in 25 fractions over 5 weeks, concurrently with capecitabine [chemoradiotherapy; CRT]). Total mesorectal excision was undertaken 6-8 weeks after preoperative treatment, with two additional cycles of CAPOX (intravenous oxaliplatin [130 mg/m 2 , once a day] on day 1 and capecitabine [1,000 mg/m 2 , twice a day] from days 1 to 14) in the TNT group and six cycles of CAPOX in the CRT group. The primary end point was 3-year disease-free survival (DFS). RESULTS Between August 2015 and August 2018, a total of 599 patients were randomly assigned to receive TNT (n = 302) or CRT (n = 297). At a median follow-up of 35.0 months, 3-year DFS was 64.5% and 62.3% in TNT and CRT groups, respectively (hazard ratio, 0.883; one-sided 95% CI, not applicable to 1.11; P < .001 for noninferiority). There was no significant difference in metastasis-free survival or locoregional recurrence, but the TNT group had better 3-year overall survival than the CRT group (86.5% v 75.1%; P = .033). Treatment effects on DFS and overall survival were similar regardless of prognostic factors. The prevalence of acute grade III-V toxicities during preoperative treatment was 26.5% in the TNT group versus 12.6% in the CRT group ( P < .001). CONCLUSION Short-term radiotherapy with preoperative chemotherapy followed by surgery was efficacious with acceptable toxicity and could be used as an alternative to CRT for locally advanced rectal cancer.

papers.title: Total Neoadjuvant Therapy With Long-Course RT and Uninterrupted Doublet Chemo Offers Efficacy Benefits in High-Risk Locally Advanced Rectal Cancer
